state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process`, `Core\Process\Handle`, `Core\Process\Result` and `Core\Program` are green. `Core\Queue`, `Core\Queue\Id` and `Core\Queue\Stats` have class cards (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/queue.rs`), and every member card of the three is in the plain voice. `Core\Queue::push`, `status`, `cancel` and `delete` have all their feature proofs, with perf recorded. Each of the six `Core\Queue` members has a Rust `covers:` marker in `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/queue_sqlite.rs`.

`stats` and `purge` still owe about, three examples, an attack and a bench each. `Core\Queue\Stats`'s five members owe every proof, tests included (`bun nv proofs --group 'Core\Queue\Stats'`).

The floor regression after the previous session (`worker::tests::a_job_pushed_to_a_server_with_one_worker_reaches_succeeded`) was two runs of the `nvs` test binary sharing one SQLite file under `temp_dir()`. Both fixture paths in `crates/nvs-cli/src/worker.rs` now carry the process id.

The shape every `Core\Queue` proof uses (an in-memory SQLite block, tables created by the program) is a playbook bullet under *Writing a test case*. Copy `docs/examples/core/Queue/status/nvs.toml` into each new member directory and into `tests/hostile/core/Queue/<member>/`. A member needing `queue.purge` adds `[capabilities.queue] purge = [...]`, as `docs/examples/core/Queue/delete/nvs.toml` does. The benches share `benches/members/core/Queue/nvs.toml`, which grants `purge` on `exports`. `bun nv proofs --record-perf` takes one `--id`; a second one replaces the first.

items.text: **`Core\Queue::stats` and `Core\Queue::purge`** — about, three examples, attack and bench each. `purge` needs the `queue.purge` grant for the queue it names, and `nvs check` reads a literal queue name against it. The `stats` attack should overwrite `attempts` with text, to test whether the count throws or crashes. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/queue.rs:2319` `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/queue.rs:2375`

**`Core\Queue\Stats`'s five members** — each owes tests from Novis and Rust, examples, perf and an attack, unless a policy entry credits them to `stats`. Read `data/proofs/policy.json` for how another value class's methods were handled first. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/queue.rs:2539`

backlog: `Core\Queue::delete` deletes a row whose `state` cell has text, because only a claimed row is protected. It is not a crash; if that is wrong, `docs/decisions/0153.md` owns the answer.
